summary: Architecture-level threat model for the example token service, covering credential handling, token issuance, and signing-key custody.

in_scope: The public token endpoint and its request path.
Signing-key storage and retrieval by the token service.
out_of_scope: Downstream resource servers that consume issued tokens.
Physical security of the hosting facility.

assumptions.statement: Transport security terminates at the public edge and is correctly configured.
assumptions.effect: If it does not hold, every boundary guarantee that relies on channel confidentiality is void.

open_questions: Whether dedicated key custody hardware lands before the first production release.

components.name: Public edge proxy
components.purpose: Terminates transport security and forwards requests to the token service.

components.name: Token service
components.purpose: Authenticates clients and issues signed tokens.

components.name: Key store
components.purpose: Holds the private keys that sign issued tokens.

actors.name: Anonymous client
actors.description: Any party that can reach the public token endpoint.

actors.name: Platform operator
actors.description: Staff with host-level access to the application and restricted zones.

capabilities: Send arbitrary requests to any publicly reachable endpoint.
Replay credentials obtained from an unrelated breach.
Observe traffic on the public network.
non_capabilities: Obtain physical access to the hosting facility.

assets.name: Client credentials
assets.description: Registered client secrets and authentication material.
assets.objective: Confidentiality and resistance to offline guessing.

assets.name: Token signing keys
assets.description: Private keys that sign issued tokens.
assets.objective: Confidentiality and non-repudiation of issued tokens.

trust_boundaries.name: Public network to token endpoint
trust_boundaries.description: Requests crossing from the public network into the token service.
security_guarantees: Client credentials are never accepted over an insecure channel.
Authentication failures are rate limited per client.
validation: Negative tests assert that plaintext requests are rejected.

trust_boundaries.name: Token service to key store
trust_boundaries.description: Signing-key retrieval crossing into the restricted zone.
security_guarantees: Only the token service identity may retrieve signing keys.
validation: Integration tests assert that an unauthenticated caller is refused.

data_flows.name: Token issuance
sequence: Client presents credentials to the public edge proxy.
Proxy forwards the authenticated request to the token service.
Token service validates the credentials and issues a signed token.

data_flows.name: Signing-key retrieval
sequence: Token service requests the active signing key.
Key store authorises the caller and returns the key material.

entry_points.notes: The only unauthenticated surface in the model.

entry_points.reached: From the token service inside the application zone.
entry_points.notes: Reachable only after a foothold in the application zone.

decisions.title: Terminate transport security at the public edge

risks.title: Insider access to signing key material
Discovery metadata served over an insecure channel

controls.title: Per-client authentication rate limiting
controls.description: Bounds the rate of authentication attempts per registered client.
controls.implementation_note: Enforced at the token service rather than the edge so it survives a proxy bypass.

controls.title: Audited, identity-bound signing-key retrieval
controls.description: Restricts key retrieval to the token service identity and records every access.
controls.implementation_note: Depends on the key custody decision recorded in ADR-102.

controls.title: Discovery metadata served over TLS only
controls.description: Refuses to serve discovery metadata over an insecure channel rather than answering the request.
controls.implementation_note: Enforced at the public edge, where ADR-101 terminates transport security.

planned_evidence.title: Token endpoint negative suite
planned_evidence.description: Exercises credential replay and rate-limit exhaustion against the token endpoint.

planned_evidence.title: Key custody integration suite
planned_evidence.description: Asserts that unauthorised callers cannot retrieve signing keys and that access is audited.

planned_evidence.title: Discovery transport negative suite
planned_evidence.description: Asserts that a plaintext discovery request is refused rather than answered with metadata.

redaction: Client secrets must never be logged.
Issued token values must never be logged.
observability.alert_condition: Authentication failures for one client exceed the configured threshold within five minutes.

threats.title: Credential stuffing against the token endpoint
threats.source: An unauthenticated party on the public network.
threats.prerequisites: Possession of credentials leaked from an unrelated breach.
threats.action: Replay leaked client credentials against the token endpoint until one succeeds.
threats.impact: Issuance of valid tokens to an attacker-controlled client.
abuse_path: Obtain a credential dump from an unrelated breach.
Enumerate the public token endpoint for accepted client identifiers.
Replay each credential until the endpoint issues a token.
threats.likelihood_rationale: The endpoint is publicly reachable and credential dumps are widely available.
threats.impact_rationale: A successful replay yields a valid token indistinguishable from a legitimate one.
threats.residual_risk: Low-rate distributed replay remains possible until anomaly detection lands.
threats.existing_controls: None; the endpoint is not yet built.
threats.gaps: No rate limiting and no credential-breach screening.
threats.recommended_mitigations: Per-client rate limiting plus screening against known-breached credentials.
threats.detection_ideas: Alert on authentication failure rate per client identifier.

threats.title: Signing-key exfiltration by a platform insider
threats.source: An operator with host-level access to the application zone.
threats.prerequisites: Legitimate administrative access to the token service host.
threats.action: Read the retrieved signing key material from process memory or configuration.
threats.impact: Ability to mint tokens indefinitely without detection.
abuse_path: Authenticate to the token service host with administrative credentials.
Trigger or observe a signing-key retrieval.
Copy the key material out of the restricted zone.
threats.likelihood_rationale: Requires an authorised operator to act maliciously.
threats.impact_rationale: Stolen signing keys forge tokens that no downstream check can distinguish.
threats.treatment_rationale: Host-level insider access is accepted until dedicated key custody hardware lands.
threats.residual_risk: Full insider compromise of signing keys remains accepted and is tracked as R1.
threats.existing_controls: Access to the restricted zone is limited to named operators.
threats.gaps: Key material is retrievable in plaintext by any process on the host.
threats.recommended_mitigations: Move signing operations behind dedicated custody hardware.
threats.detection_ideas: Audit and alert on signing-key retrievals outside expected rotation windows.

threats.title: Metadata downgrade over plain HTTP
threats.source: A network attacker positioned between the client and the public edge.
threats.prerequisites: The ability to observe and modify traffic on the public network.
threats.action: Serve tampered discovery metadata over an insecure channel.
threats.impact: Clients are steered to an attacker-controlled token endpoint.
abuse_path: Intercept a client's plaintext discovery request.
Return metadata naming an attacker-controlled token endpoint.
Collect credentials the client presents to that endpoint.
threats.likelihood_rationale: Requires a network position, which is routine on hostile access networks.
threats.impact_rationale: Credentials are exposed, but only for clients that accept insecure discovery.
threats.residual_risk: Clients that ignore transport errors remain exposed and are tracked as R2.
threats.existing_controls: None in place; CTRL-003 is planned and discovery is not yet published.
threats.gaps: RFCX-001 requires metadata over TLS, but nothing enforces it while CTRL-003 remains planned.
threats.recommended_mitigations: Refuse to serve discovery metadata over an insecure channel.
threats.detection_ideas: Alert on any plaintext request reaching the discovery path.

supersessions.rationale: Split credential replay out of the combined endpoint-abuse threat.
